title: POS, cards and ATMs: pay, withdraw and fix failed payments

say: POS, cards and ATMs: pay, withdraw and fix failed payments.
This is the video for module 3 of Digital Payments and POS Basics.
POS means point of sale. The machine asks your bank for permission, and your bank approves or declines.
Most problems come from rushing, letting someone else handle your card, or not checking the amount.

say: You will learn a safe card routine, how to read a receipt, how to use an ATM, how float works, and what to do when a payment fails.

say: For example, Ruth's supermarket payment of 23,750 naira prints a DECLINED receipt, then an APPROVED one. Only APPROVED means money went through.

panel.heading: Only APPROVED means you paid
items: Status: APPROVED or DECLINED
Amount: exactly what you agreed
Terminal ID: that exact machine
RRN and STAN: reference numbers

say: She checks her app before leaving and sees one debit, not two. She keeps both receipts, because the terminal ID, RRN and STAN are what her bank needs to trace a payment.

say: Kemi's app showed a separate charge line for each withdrawal. So she listed what she really needs cash for each week.
Transport, about 7,000 naira. Market items, about 10,000. Small extras, about 3,000.
That is 20,000. Now she makes one withdrawal on Monday from her own bank's ATM, and keeps half at home so she does not carry it all. Read any fee notice on the screen before you confirm.
Use an ATM at a bank branch, in daylight. Never accept help from a stranger. If you need help, go inside the bank.

cards.d: Never accept help at an ATM, even from someone who says he works there.
Stay at the machine. Call your bank's official number and block the card.
Loose, glued or extra-thick slot or keypad? Do not use that machine.

say: If the machine keeps your card, do not walk away. Call your bank's saved number from where you stand and block the card.

say: Before you insert your card, look at the slot and keypad. If anything looks loose or glued on, use another machine. And always take your card first, then your cash.

say: Float is cash in your drawer plus money in your agent account. Zainab starts with 150,000 cash and 100,000 in her account.
When a customer withdraws, her cash goes down and her account goes up. When a customer gives cash to send, the opposite happens.

say: After three customers she has 110,000 in cash and 140,000 in her account.

say: Still 250,000 in total. Her charges of 2,400 sit in a separate envelope, so she knows exactly what she earned.
Never give out cash until the terminal prints APPROVED and your app shows the credit.

say: For example, Ebere in Aba tries to withdraw 30,000 naira at a POS agent. It prints DECLINED, but she gets a debit alert. She does not let the agent try again.

panel.heading: Debited but no cash
items: Do not try the same payment again
Check your history for a reversal
Keep the receipt and references
Complain to your own bank, get a reference
Follow up, then escalate
panel.rule: Do not repeat a failed payment. You may be debited twice.

say: She checks her app for a reversal and photographs the declined receipt with its terminal ID, RRN and STAN.

say: She checks daily until the 30,000 returns. If your bank does not resolve it, escalate within the bank, then to the CBN's consumer protection channel. Real banks never ask for your PIN or OTP.

say: To remember. Count the digits before your PIN. Only APPROVED means you paid. Never accept help at an ATM. Float is cash plus account balance. And when a payment fails, do not repeat it. Call your own bank with your receipt.

panel.heading: Remember
items: Count the digits on screen before your PIN
Only a receipt marked APPROVED means you paid
Never accept help from strangers at an ATM
Float is cash plus account balance
Failed payment: do not repeat, call your bank
